item.title: Growing Debt Burden By Tinubu Will Be Passed To Future Generation — NDC
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has called on Nigerians to turn out in massive numbers in the 2027 elections and use their votes to demand accountability, fiscal responsibility, and a government that puts the people’s interests first, according to a statement by the party’s National Presidential Campaign Council Spokesperson, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu. The party said the country’s growing debt burden, in light of new loan requests by President Bola Tinubu, and the obligations being passed on to future generations, make the 2027 general election too important for citizens to sit out. The Party’s plea followed President Tinubu again, asking the National Assembly to approve a new external borrowing plan of $7.7 billion (approximately ₦10.79 trillion) to help finance the 2026 budget deficit. “…making this a case of one week, new loan”, the statement said partly. Ikokwu noted that the party’s passionate appeal to Nigerians is to turn out massively and vote for Peter Obi and Engr. Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on January 16, 2027, just as Americans demonstrated the power of the ballot in their November 4, 2026 elections. NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, says he will serve for only one term of four years if elected President in 2027. She observed that Americans, like Nigerians, are grappling with the high cost of living and economic hardship. Rather than merely grumbling or resigning themselves to their circumstances, she said, Americans turned out to exercise their democratic rights, demonstrating that the power to change government ultimately rests with the electorate. Dr Ikokwu therefore urged Nigerians to emulate Americans, whom she described as champions of democratic participation, by coming out in their millions to vote for Obi and Kwankwaso. Dr Ikokwu said: “Truly, it seems that right now, we cannot stop President Tinubu from his One Week! New Loan! One Week! New Loan! borrowing spree, which is already hitting the roof, because, regrettably, he has pocketed the National Assembly. We seem to have a rubber-stamp legislature that, before a loan request formally gets to its desk, it has already been endorsed. “But Nigerians should not despair. The ballot remains our most powerful instrument of change. We appeal to citizens to use their votes to rescue the country from this debt trap and entrust its future to a government committed to transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources.” The NDC reiterated that the country’s economic future must not be mortgaged by unsustainable borrowing and the mismanagement of public resources. item.title: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel doesn’t sound thrilled about catching up with Tom Brady before he calls Packers game
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Patriots’ Mike Vrabel doesn’t sound thrilled about catching up with Tom Brady before he calls Packers game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Tom Brady will return to Gillette Stadium on Sunday, but this time he won’t be wearing a Patriots uniform. The seven-time Super Bowl champion will be at the stadium as a FOX Sports broadcaster for New England ‘s Week 9 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. His return also gives former teammates a chance to reconnect. However, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel did not sound particularly excited when asked about catching up with Brady. “I think I’m required contractually to catch up with him at some point,” Vrabel joked during Wednesday’s press conference. “I’m sure it’ll be a Zoom. I’m sure they won’t show up here. I’m sure it will be on Zoom.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Vrabel added that he expected to see Brady at Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots Hall of Fame induction on Saturday. Gronkowski, who also works for FOX Sports, will be honored at Gillette Stadium. Vrabel and Brady spent eight seasons together in New England from 2001 to 2008, winning three Super Bowls. Their relationship has remained friendly since their playing days ended. Vrabel previously described Brady as a friend and confirmed that they exchanged texts after Super Bowl LX. Brady has also spoken about returning to the stadium, admitting the occasion will bring back plenty of memories. “It’ll be certainly emotional,” Brady said. He recalled the memorable games and championship moments he experienced at Gillette Stadium and praised the Patriots organization. Sunday will mark Brady’s first appearance at the venue as a FOX Sports broadcaster . He previously returned for his Patriots Hall of Fame induction in 2024 and the unveiling of his statue in 2025. The reunion will bring several familiar faces together again, even if Vrabel’s scheduled conversation with his former quarterback may have to happen over Zoom. item.title: Lakers face fresh Bronny James roster questions after former No. 1 pick’s explosive criticism
item.description: Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images Kwame Brown has delivered a brutal assessment of Bronny James’ place on the Los Angeles Lakers roster, questioning why the third-year guard continues to occupy an NBA spot. The former No. 1 overall pick believes Bronny has taken an opportunity away from another player who worked hard to reach the league, with LeBron James’ influence central to his criticism. The Lakers have made a strong start to the 2026-27 season, sitting at 6-2 after eight games. However, Bronny has featured in just four of those contests, playing only 11 minutes in total. Kwame Brown questions Bronny James’ place on the Los Angeles Lakers roster Speaking on his YouTube channel, Brown did not hold back when discussing Bronny’s limited contributions and the circumstances surrounding his place in the team. The former Lakers teammate of Kobe Bryant said: “This is the National Basketball Association. This ain’t for the little boys and wimps. This is professional, and what I saw, I just don’t get it. It’s mind-blowing how somebody lost a job to that. Some kid that worked their b*** off, that really feels like they could have made the NBA, they lost their job to that. And the only reason why everybody is okay with it is because of his father. This is a shame, what we’re actually seeing. Call it hate, call it whatever you want. To me it’s a shame.” Brown’s comments followed two difficult appearances for Bronny. Against the Toronto Raptors, he finished with no points, one turnover and a minus-11 rating in roughly two minutes. His next outing against the Miami Heat brought two points from a single made shot, but he played for only around a minute. Brown was equally unimpressed, describing the brief spell against Miami as: “the worst 90 seconds of basketball I ever seen in my life.” The criticism comes as the Lakers look to maximise Luka Doncic’s prime years. The Athletic’s Jovan Buha has suggested the franchise could consider moving on from Bronny or Jaden Hardy to create roster flexibility. Bronny is earning $2.3 million this season and has a team option for 2027-28. With his role still limited under JJ Redick, the Lakers face growing questions about whether his roster spot is the best use of their available resources. item.title: Savannah teams and runners to watch in GHSA Cross Country state meets
item.description: The GHSA State Cross Country Championships are here as races are set to be run in Carrollton on Friday and Saturday, Nov. 6 and 7. Runners and teams have been under the watchful eye of their coaches as they have been focused on peaking at the right time for the end-of-the-season event. Richmond Hill coach Levi Sybert has his girls and boys teams ready for the Class 7A meet, which will be run on Saturday, after both squads finished second in the Class 7A Sectional teams standings. The boys were led by freshman sensation Liam Penttila, who ran a personal best time of 15:44.22 on the 3.1 mile course to finish second in the race individually. Wildcat senior Eddie Howell was eighth in 16:23.58, one spot ahead of his sophomore teammate Caden Gross who finished in 16:30.29. Junior Derek Feske was 15th in 16:59.91. Junior Chloe Miller led the Wildcat girls with a third place finish in 18:50.02, with senior Gabriella Francis fifth in 19:30.21. Senior Julia Anastasio was 11th in 19:47.30, one place ahead of freshman Lucy Puskar (20:08.71). "Liam (Penttila) is just a freshman but he has a lot of ability and has found his stride this year," Sybert said. "He's a quiet and hard working runner. He stayed in the back of the pack earlier in the year, but now he likes to get out and run with the top dogs. He's a very methodical runner. "Julia (Anastasio) is coming back from a hip injury that slowed her down as a junior and is having a big season," he said "And Chloe has emerged as our No. 1 lately, and with Gabby Francis we have a solid group at the top of our lineup." The Wildcat boys have a chance to win it all, as they did in 2021, Sybert said, and he's hoping for a podium (Top 4) finish for both squads. The Savannah Arts girls are on a quest to win their third straight state crown and took another step toward that goal by winning the Class 2A Sectional 1 meet. The Panthers were led by senior Francie Tedder, who finished second in 19:22.00. Morgan Irvine was third with a time of 20:13.60 and McKay Bennett finished fifth in 20:33.00. Madeline Balthrop was seventh in 20:52.00 and Avae Treece finished 10th in 21:34.70. The Panthers boys squad had a strong team run to finish third in the meet led by Logan Brodhead, who was fourth in 17:30.10 and Nico Klaras, who took eighth with a time of 17:37.10. The Islands girls team won the Class 3A Sectional 1 team title with three girls finishing in the Top 10. Leila Kellison was second in 20:55.90, with Zeycan Agbas sixth in 22:38.60, one spot ahead of Kaileigh Toler (22:39.00). The Class 4A, 5A and Class 2A-4A Private Schools races will be held Friday, with the Class 1A, 2A, 3A, 6A and 7A events set for Saturday. Here's a look at the area teams and their top runners who have qualified for the state meets in Carrollton with results from last week's sectional qualifying races. item.title: Missouri basketball vs SLU scout report, score prediction
item.description: For the first time in a quarter-century, Mizzou and SLU men’s basketball teams are meeting on the court. Missouri basketball, fresh off slamming Cleveland State by 61 points in its season-opener, is rolling right into the meat of its beefed-up nonconference slate, traveling for a game Friday, Nov. 6, against in-state rival Saint Louis on a neutral floor at the Enterprise Center in St. Louis. The game tips off at 6 p.m. and airs on ESPNU.The Tigers (1-0) made light work of head coach Dennis Gates’ former team in their season debut, but the warm-up period was short this year. Saint Louis (1-0), which is coached by Josh Schertz, thumped Georgia in the first round of the NCAA Tournament last season before falling to eventual national champion Michigan. Several key members from that Big Dance squad are back for more with the Billikens this year. More: Guard CJ Gunn ruled ineligible, will not play for Missouri basketball this year SLU and Mizzou have not played since December 2001. That hiatus ends Friday evening. Here’s what you need to know about SLU before Friday’s game at Enterprise Center: Will Robbie Avila be available to play for SLU? Mizzou isn’t the only team in the state with some significant November court drama. Standout forward Robbie Avila had a hearing Wednesday for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA. He needs the court order to be able to play for the Billikens this season. Avila was the leading scorer on the SLU team that won 29 games, won the Atlantic-10 regular season title and went to the second round of the NCAA Tournament last season. The 6-foot-10 forward averaged 12.8 points and 4.1 assists per game and shot 41.0% from 3-point range. He’s a difference-maker. The judge indicated that a ruling should come soon. Saint Louis head coach Josh Schertz said that if the result is favorable for Avila, he will play the forward against Missouri . Change on this front could come at any time, so keep your eyes peeled. Son of former Tigers star is SLU starter The son of the Big Eight Freshman of the Year and Mizzou alum Kelly Thames will face his father’s alma mater this coming Friday. And Kellen Thames is going to be a real challenge for Mizzou to defend. The high-motor fifth-year guard, listed at 6-6, shot 6-of-6 from the field in SLU’s season-opening win over Lehigh for 15 points and added six rebounds. He’s excellent at getting out in transition and attacking downhill. The Billikens scored 50 points in the paint against Lehigh. They’re going to give Mizzou a test on the interior, and Thames is going to be leading that effort. His father played 128 games for Mizzou between 1993-98 under Norm Stewart and averaged 17.6 points and 8.2 rebounds in his career. He is eighth on MU’s all-time career-points list with 1,689. Player to watch: Trey Green How Missouri is able to defend Green is going to be interesting. We’re curious to see what Mizzou’s massive lineup will look like against a smaller, quicker guard. item.title: Players to watch, predictions as Notre Dame football faces Miami (Fla.)
item.description: SOUTH BEND – Welcome to an impossible exercise for a showdown of two Top 10 teams that carry serious national championship aspirations on what might be one of those nights for Notre Dame football inside Notre Dame Stadium. Here we pinpoint four players to watch, but four is nowhere enough. Eight might not be. Even a dozen might still be too small a number. There are big-time players capable of making big-time plays across each sideline in this one. The quarterbacks. The linebackers. The running backs. The interior lines. Heck, even the head coaches should be ones to watch. We see you, Mario and Marcus. Who do you track in this one? Who don't you? Keep your head on a swivel while trying to see this guy and that guy and those guys. Let's at least start with these four and go from there. You've been warned. There's talent everywhere in this one. Who will deliver? UM, ND 411: Notre Dame football vs. Miami | How to watch, game time Analysis: Showdown with Miami will require vintage CJ Carr for Notre Dame No. 1 MIAMI HURRICANES (8-0) DB Omar Thornton (0) The step up in competition seems to suit the Carver Ranches, Florida native just fine, thank you. Same goes from stepping from the college football shadows into the white-hot spotlight for a program barreling toward a possible return to the national championship game. The 5-foot-11, 201-pound Thornton spent two years in anonymity up there at Boston College , where he produced at an All-Atlantic Coast Conference level. Thornton played in 23 games with 14 starts with the Eagles, where he tallied 111 tackles. Last year in Chestnut Hill, Mass., he made a team-high nine stops against Notre Dame. So, he knows the Irish. Coming off a season high eight tackles against Clemson, Thornton has been relatively quiet the last three weeks. He's made only five stops, including just one last weekend at North Carolina. The former high school linebacker has found ways to affect games other than tackles. He's second on the Hurricanes ' 28 th ranked defense in tackles for loss (6.5) and first for quarterback hurries (five). He has three sacks. He handles his business on the back end of the defense and handles business at the line of scrimmage. WR Malachi Toney (1) Toney announced his arrival on the college football big stage not so subtly last season as a true freshman when the 5-11, 183-pounder from Liberty City caught 109 passes for 1,211 yards and 10 touchdowns. Guess what? He might be better as a sophomore. Seriously, why isn't Toney getting more Heisman Tropy love? Through eight games, Tony has tallied 73 catches for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns. He averages 14.1 yards per catch. He averages nine catches for 128 yards per game. He gets game planned by every opposing defensive coordinator yet still finds room to roam in secondaries and down the sidelines and, most importantly, into end zones. item.title: 39 Years Later, Calvin And Hobbes' Best Quote On Grief Is Still a Heartbreaking Classic
item.description: Most of the time, Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes was a straightforward comedy, set in equal parts a nondescript American suburb and its protagonist's imagination. While it's got more than its share of memorable lines and genuine wisdom, C&H was rarely out to tug on anyone's heartstrings. There are two exceptions to that rule. One is a full story arc from March 1987, in which Calvin tries to rescue a baby raccoon. The other is a one-shot from late in the comic's run, as one of Watterson's more experimental Sunday strips. Both are quiet meditations on death, as Calvin confronts mortality through encounters with animals.

item.title: In Gallery: More Than The AI Conversations – See Some of The Beautiful Faces at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026
item.description: In Dakar, for Goalkeepers 2026 , professionals from various industries converged in a hall on the 29th of October, 2026, to discuss how Africans are already leveraging AI to solve social problems, and to also explore further opportunities. Themed “ Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth “, the conversations weren’t all about using AI to build an equitable future; there were performances, including one from the legendary Youssou N’Dour , and the attendees also showed up and showed out in different styles and fashions. The event was attended by several influential figures, including Nigeria’s Tsakute Ladi Jonah (popularly known as Saskay), Fatou Jupiter Toure , Mamadou Ly , and Fatma Samoura , the former diplomat and senior executive who became the first female Secretary General of FIFA. Other notable attendees included Karim Sy , the entrepreneur and founder of Jokkolabs, and Dr Seydina Ndiaye , an AI expert at the UN High-Level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence and the principal investigator of the AI Living Lab for Innovative and Viable Ethical Policies and Systems (ALIVE Lab), among others. item.title: Zeeland West vs Battle Creek Central playoff scouting report and prediction
item.description: The second week of the playoffs is here and the Holland area has just one high school team that advanced to the district finals. Here is a look at the matchup in the MHSAA playoffs. More: Zeeland West football rolls past Niles without star running back to advance Battle Creek Central at Zeeland West WHEN: 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6 WHERE: Zeeland Stadium RECORDS: Zeeland West 8-2, Battle Creek Central 6-4 PLAYOFF APPERANCES: Zeeland West 22, Battle Creek Central 14 LAST WEEK: Zeeland West beat Niles 60-27, Battle Creek Central beat Battle Creek Harper Creek 41-38 LAST MEETING: First meeting SERIES HISTORY: First meeting SCOUTING REPORT ON BCC: Battle Creek Central only played eight games in the regular season, yet averaged 41 points per game. That was a school record for points per game, passing the 2001 undefeated BCC team which scored 38.5 points per game in the regular season. … Despite missing some time due to injury, junior quarterback Lee Campbell Jr. has nearly 1,000 yards passing and 1,000 yards rushing in basically six outings. In the regular season, Campbell had 922 yards passing and seven touchdown passes. He also has 995 yards rushing and 19 touchdowns. Junior running back Mubarrack Jubril has 1,096 yards rushing and 17 touchdowns. BCC's top receiver, Sir Paris, had 409 yards receiving and three more touchdowns. … In Week 3, BCC and Mattawan scored the most combined points ever in the state of Michigan in 11-player football. Mattawan beat BCC 77-76 in five overtimes. SCOUTING REPORT ON ZW: Running back Brandon Holman missed the first round of the playoffs with an ankle injury. He is expected back this week and will be a key part of the offense. … The Dux run a Wing-T and Power-T offense with double tight ends and three running backs. The offense is an option style and in most plays is decided by how the defense plays it. They have become a state power by finessing this process so defenses and often fans don't know who actually has the ball. … Quarterback Drew Albrecht is the signal caller and is essentially a fourth running back, making it very difficult to plan for four points of attack. He can also throw and it is almost always out of the same formation, so it either will go to a tight end or someone out of the backfield. … The Dux always go for two after a touchdown. Always. The last time they attempted an extra point or a field goal was more than a decade ago. Statistically if the achieve it 50% of the time, they are breaking even, but they average higher than that, giving them an advantage. PREDICTION: Zeeland West 28, Battle Creek Central 14. item.title: The real Hope-Calvin football rivalry begins this week in undefeated clash
item.description: The introduction to the Hope-Calvin football rivalry has come and gone. This year, the real rivalry begins. The first two years, Calvin didn't have a home stadium and had the expected growing pains that any new program would face. Hope was also the dominant force in the MIAA which has led to a couple of pretty lopsided victories for the Flying Dutch. The rivalry will be different this year. Both teams enter the showdown 7-0, tied for first place in the MIAA after the Knights beat Trine 51-20 on Halloween and Hope similarly crushed Kalamazoo. The win over 6-1 Trine proved that Calvin is for real this year, not just beating mediocre teams. Now the Knights will host Hope for the first time in their very own stadium at 1 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 7. Calvin passing attack It has been all about passing for the Knights, who put up 400 yards through the air to quiet the Thunder. They rushed for just 89 yards on 32 carries, but were able to pass at will. Thomas Vaccaro was 23-for-34 passing with four touchdowns. Hunter Hogan and Luke Michmerhuizen each had more than 100 yards receiving. That is a lot to defend. But Hope's secondary has been strong this year, too, and this could be the battle for the game. If Hope can even slow down Calvin's passing attack it would be a huge lift and possible key to victory. Hope defensive line rules One of the big components to The Rivalry so far has been Hope's dominance of the line of scrimmage. While the Knights will be better than in years past on the line, Hope has one of the top D-lines in the country, which could make a huge difference. If Hope can rush Vaccaro and force him to make quick decisions under duress, Tate Bezeau and company will be in the backfield a lot. Hope's run game Hope continues to rush for more than 300 yards a game and slowly put its opponents to sleep. Long drives have produced a lot of short rushing touchdowns this season and that is a sign of control. Hope knows it can control the ball with long, methodical drives. The running backs don't get tired either, because Hope rotates so many in, that there are always fresh legs on the field. If hope can control the ball and limit the passing, the Flying Dutch could clinch a share of the MIAA title. Contact sports editor Dan D’Addona at Dan.D’Addona@hollandsentinel.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter @DanDAddona or Facebook @HollandSentinelSport s. item.title: Iraola: “They are Cheap Goals”
item.description: ISTANBUL, TURKEY - NOVEMBER 04: Andoni Iraola, Manager of Liverpool, reacts during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Fenerbahce SK and Liverpool FC at Fenerbahce Sükrü Saracoglu Spor Kompleksi on November 04, 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) | Getty Images Liverpool FC head coach Andoni Iraola was pretty upfront about his team’s lack of defensive nous in the 3-2 away defeat to Fenerbahce in the UEFA Champions League. In the post-match press conference, Iraola was pretty blunt about the way the game went, and refused to blame rotation as a possible reason for the lapses in concentration. Select quotes from the presser: “The main reason I can find to lose the game is we conceded [from] three set-pieces. It’s something that we were doing very well in the league, I think we were dealing [with it] quite well until today. We knew it was one of the strengths of Fenerbahce, but we concede from a free-kick, from a corner, even from the long throw at the end.” “They are goals that have hurt us because we have twice gone in front after having good moments, controlling the game, arriving. We found the goals. But after, we conceded in situations that we definitely should defend better.” On his team giving away ‘cheap’ goals… “Yes, as you say, they are cheap goals. They are messy goals. It’s a free-kick; it’s quite far also the free-kick. You know, it is through the wall, [they are] mistakes that can cost you. The last goal… it is a long throw, the first phase is control, but after a very long ball and Muriqi wins it.” “The second one is, I think Cody is the one touching the ball just in front of Ali [Alisson Becker]. In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate because it was so noisy. It was even difficult for me to give any kind of instruction. It was, I suppose, difficult there, the communication between Ali and Cody.” On making five changes to his XI… “We’ve done this not just today. We’ve been doing it all season and all the games we’ve played midweek. I think we’ve been changing at least four, five, six, seven players. Because of the schedule that we have, it’s impossible to maintain with always the [same] starting XI. I think we have been dealing well with these rotations. I trust the squad to sustain the level.” “I don’t think it was the main reason why we lost, I think some of the players that didn’t play on the weekend have played a good game. We have to look more at how we conceded the goals [and] the reason why we didn’t win because after I think we had good moments, especially on the ball where we could score our two goals.” On if conceding overall control or whether the way the goals were conceded was more frustrating for him… “I think we had, before scoring the goals, some very good moments on the ball. item.title: Time is right for Conlan-backed Hale to flip the page
item.description: Hale's last bout as an amateur was defeat by Patris Mughalzai at the Commonwealth Games [Getty Images] Leaving amateur boxing behind to pursue a professional career was not a tough decision for Belfast's John Paul Hale. An Irish Elite champion in 2021, Hale also collected six Ulster titles and competed at the 2022 and 2026 Commonwealth Games, so the 25-year-old felt "I did as much as I could in the amateur game and now is the right time". Of course, signing off with a medal from this summer's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow would have been ideal, but it wasn't to be as Hale exited the ring frustrated after his opening round defeat by England's Patris Mughalzai in a bout he was docked two points to his opponent's one. Boxing, whichever the code, remains a subjective sport when it comes to officiating, and Hale was more than irked after that loss, his one-finger salute to the officials telling its own story - the same finger that his new manager Michael Conlan flipped in Rio in 2016 when dealing with his own disappointment. "It's a weird one as it's the first time I wasn't upset at myself," Hale told BBC Sport NI when reflecting on that July day. "I knew how hard I had worked before it and had beaten that lad [Mughalzai] before. That time, the referee was letting me work instead of calling 'break' and if he was holding, there were warnings. "I went into that [Commonwealth Games bout] with a mindset that it would be a similar outcome but just felt the referee took it away from me. "It was upsetting because deep down, I knew it was my last opportunity to accomplish what I set out to do [as an amateur]." Same old issues persist in the amateur code While Conlan's reverse to Vladimir Nikitin at the 2016 Olympics would cause outrage and set the wheels in motion for the downfall of amateur boxing's-then ruling body, AIBA [since rebranded to IBA]. World Boxing's approval by the International Olympic Committee has resulted in an exodus to the new body who oversaw the Commonwealth Game but while administration has changed, Hale feels some of the old problems remain. "I don't feel it has changed even though there has been the transition to World Boxing," he opined. "It seemed they [judges] were looking for more aggressive fighters and that suited me, but it didn't feel that way and it just feels like nothing has changed. "When you get to the elite-level fighters, you have different styles they need to sort out how they want people to fight to win. Some can win on the back foot and are not getting the decisions, then others go forward and aren't getting it. "Look at Jude Gallagher at the Commonwealth Games . Loads of others were sickened by it too, a few Scottish fighters were on the end of bad ones [decisions]." Conlan's backing a major boost Conlan twice challenged for professional world honours after a stellar amateur career [Getty Images] There was no temptation to stay amateur and have a crack at reaching the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles despite toying

item.title: New Bayern deal makes Kane Europe's best-paid player
item.description: New Bayern deal makes Kane Europe's best-paid player After several rounds of negotiations, Bayern Munich finally announced on Thursday that Harry Kane had signed a new contract running until 2029. According to Sky Germany and AZ, Kane will earn a club-record salary, surpassing his previous €25 million per year. The new deal is the most lucrative in Bayern's history, with sources telling The Athletic's David Ornstein that the 33-year-old is now the highest-paid player in European football in terms of guaranteed salary, although some players are thought to be able to earn more overall when bonuses are included. Ornstein also reports that, despite Kane now being 33, Bayern don't see this as his final contract with the club. According to AZ, Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen held eight rounds of negotiations with the striker's father and brother before finally getting the deal over the line. Kane and his representatives reportedly wanted a contract until 2030, or at least an option to extend the deal until then. However, according to AZ, the final agreement doesn't include such an option. In return, Bayern made concessions to the striker in other areas, including his salary and image rights.

item.title: Dybala to undergo more tests, Gollini set for return
item.description: Dybala to undergo more tests, Gollini set for return Roma wants to immediately erase the disappointment of their Champions League defeat at Manchester United (3-2) and focus on their undefeated league campaign. The Roman side will host Aquilani’s Sassuolo on Saturday at 8:45 PM, a team that is experiencing a poor record: four consecutive defeats against Frosinone, Como, Lazio, and Fiorentina. Ahead of the final match before the break, Gian Piero Gasperini hopes to recover at least one of the players currently injured: Dybala, Koné, and Gollini. Svilar and Pellegrini are unlikely to return. It’s a crucial day for Paulo Dybala. As La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, the Argentine striker will undergo a crucial test today to determine whether his calf problem has resolved. Manu Koné appears to have already overcome his respective physical issues, but Roma will be extremely cautious. There is optimism regarding Gollini’s recovery, given that he was experiencing less back pain yesterday. If he misses again, Gasperini will keep Vasquez from the start, as he did at Old Trafford against Manchester United. Svilar, Pellegrini, and Rensch are unlikely to return before the break.

item.title: 1980 F1 world champion Alan Jones dies aged 80
item.description: Motorsport photo The 1980 World Drivers’ Champion, Australia’s Alan Jones, died on the Gold Coast on Thursday. In a statement released on behalf of Jones's family, his wife, Amanda Butler-Davis, said he died following a short illness. He was 80. “We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness,” Butler-Davis said. “He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for. “Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way. “Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe. “As a family, we would like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who was part of Alan's journey for the many years of friendship, love and support. He was incredibly fortunate to have so many wonderful people around him.” Jones was born in Melbourne in 1946, the son of businessman and racer Stan Jones, and watched from the sidelines when his father won the 1959 Australian Grand Prix at Longford. The younger Jones repeated the feat at Calder Park in 1980 and remains the last Australian driver to have won the race, which is considered the second-oldest Grand Prix in the world. Jones dabbled in racing in the UK in the 1960s before returning to Australia, before he moved to London in 1970. It took three years for him to establish himself, winning his first Formula 3 race at Silverstone in 1973, the same year he took second in the British F3 championship in a GRD. Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones In 1975 he made his Formula 1 debut at the Spanish Grand Prix, in a Hesketh, and when that team shut at the end of the season he moved to Graham Hill’s team, then to Surtees. That team also was to close and Jones’s career looked to have stalled – until Shadow called, having lost lead driver Tom Pryce in a tragic crash in South Africa. In a fairytale result, Jones won in Austria, after a brilliant drive on a wet track, passing local hero Niki Lauda on the way to the first win for an Australian since the retirement of Sir Jack Brabham. Ferrari sounded Jones out for 1978 and Jones thought he had a deal – until Enzo Ferrari reneged, and signed Gilles Villeneuve. Jones was left with an offer from the lowly Williams team, for which owners Frank Williams and Patrick Head had big plans. Jones nearly took the Williams FW06 to the win at Long Beach, but for a broken wing, then again at Brands Hatch, where a gearbox broke. In the US Grand Prix, he was second to Carlos Reutemann’s Ferrari while a new car, the FW07, was being finished back at Grove. Once Jones and new team-mate Clay Regazzoni got their hands on the car, they looked like winners nearly immediately. Jones led by a mile at Silvers

item.title: UPDATED ODDS: Notre Dame is more than a touchdown favorite over Miami
item.description: PROVO, UT - OCTOBER 17: Guerby Lambert #76 and Jonaz Walton #20 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish run off the field after scoring against the Brigham Young Cougars during the second half of their game at LaVell Edwards Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Provo, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The time has finally come for what could be the college football game of the year. This Saturday, the No. 1 ranked Miami Hurricanes take their perfect record to South Bend for a prime time matchup against the No. 4 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a game that’s likely to have a massive impact on the college football playoff. The news of Malachi Toney’s injury has made its way to the bookmakers, and the Irish are now more than a touchdown favorite over Miami. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, Notre Dame is currently a 7.5 point favorite over Miami with an over/under of 57.5 points. ESPN’s college gameday will be there, but the real jewel here is that the Irish already have one loss this season, so this could very well be a playoff game to get into the playoff. Miami is coming off of back-to-back close game performances against unranked Florida State and unranked North Carolina — where the officiating was a major topic after both games as well. You’d be foolish, however, to think Miami won’t dial up their best game of the season in what will be their biggest regular season game since they opened up the 2025 season against Notre Dame.

item.title: Rafael Benitez confirms he could return to the Premier League
item.description: Rafael Benitez confirms he could return to the Premier League Rafa Benitez Premier League Return Hinges on Finding the Right Project Rafa Benitez wants back in. That is the story, and it is not difficult to understand why. English football still suits him, the Premier League still attracts him, and the rhythm of the competition clearly still grabs him. Speaking on talkSPORT Drive, Benitez made it clear that his current UEFA role has not dulled his appetite for the dugout. If anything, it has sharpened it. He is studying elite matches across Europe, tracking tactical patterns, measuring intensity levels and keeping up with players and styles. That is not the routine of someone winding down. That is someone staying ready. His words were direct: “You know that I’m working now for UEFA, but I’m watching games all the time, and especially the Premier League, because I want to know the players, I want to know their style. “I could see the other day when I was watching Juventus vs Napoli, then I was watching Liverpool vs Arsenal, and you can see the difference. “So I like the Premier League because of the intensity. “Every game, every ball is a challenge. I think it’s fantastic. The problem is that you need to find the right project. Talking about projects in football now is quite complicated.” Premier League Appeal Remains Strong That is the crucial part. Benitez is available, interested and experienced, but he is not walking into any chaos for the sake of a comeback. He has been around too long for that. He knows the difference between a job and a structure. He also knows that too many clubs talk about long-term planning while operating week to week. When asked directly whether that project could be in the Premier League, his answer was brief and clear: “Yeah, yeah, I would be happy with that, for sure.” There is no mystery here. Benitez values control, clarity and a club that understands what it is building. That narrows the field quickly. The Premier League offers money, profile and intensity, but it also offers impatience and noise. Managers get judged fast, often without context. Pressure Building at Struggling Clubs The timing of his comments matters because several top-flight managers are under pressure. Michael Carrick has already come through a rough spell at Manchester United and bought himself breathing room with a Champions League win. Regis Le Bris is under scrutiny at Sunderland. Pierre Sage has questions to answer at Crystal Palace. Oliver Glasner has gone as far as daring Nottingham Forest to make a decision after a 2-0 loss to Brentford. That does not mean Benitez is heading to one of those clubs. It means the market may move soon, and when it does, his name will be part of the conversation. He has won major honours in England and Europe, and he has enough credibility to appeal to owners looking for experience in a difficult moment. item.title: AEK Athens manager praises Jose Mourinho after 2-3 loss to Real Madrid: ‘I have great admiration for him’
item.description: AEK Athens manager praises Jose Mourinho after 2-3 loss to Real Madrid: ‘I have great admiration for him’ AEK Athens manager Marko Nikolic praised Jose Mourinho following his side’s 3-2 Champions League defeat to Real Madrid . Despite the disappointment of Federico Valverde’s stoppage-time winner, Nikolic expressed his admiration for the Real Madrid manager and insisted his players had every reason to be proud of their performance. Speaking at his post-match press conference (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), the AEK Athens coach analysed the game, explaining that his team had entered the contest with the intention of beating Madrid. Nikolic explains his admiration for Mourinho During his comments, Mourinho’s managerial achievements earned particular recognition from Nikolic, who highlighted his success across multiple leagues and footballing cultures. “I have great admiration for Mourinho. Wherever he goes, he gets results, and he has done so in many countries. “He wins titles in all of them – not just one, but many. To receive a compliment from him is a great honour,” he began saying. Nikolic defends attacking approach against Real Madrid Marko Nikolic’s side gave Real Madrid a run for their money. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) Nikolic was equally keen to emphasise that AEK had approached the match with genuine attacking ambition. His players competed with Real Madrid throughout the encounter, but a missed opportunity during a four-on-two situation proved costly before Valverde settled the contest with a spectacular late strike. “Our approach from the start was to try to win. We didn’t take to the pitch just to manage the game or to make a good impression. “If we’d been fresher, we’d have got a different result. We squandered a four-on-two situation that could have turned the match around. “They stole the ball from us, produced an incredible strike and won,” he explained. Nikolic urges AEK Athens to build on Madrid performance Despite losing, Nikolic refused to allow the result to overshadow his players’ efforts. AEK Athens manager Marko Nikolic is content with his team’s performance. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) He praised their commitment and identified their competitive spirit as an important part of the club’s identity. “We should be proud of our performance. The lads gave it their all. When you see the team giving their all on the pitch, it’s wonderful. “That’s our hallmark and what our fans love about us. It’s impossible to perform at the same level every three days,” he said. Ultimately, he concluded by giving the strongest message possible, stating, “I’m very proud of our team. It’s a shame about the result, but we’re fighters and we’re competitive. “We have no intention of feeling sorry for ourselves. It’s an opportunity to build something better. We’ve still got a long way to go,” he concluded.

item.title: Unai Emery Open To New Deal As Aston Villa Make Big Statement
item.description: Unai Emery Open To New Deal As Aston Villa Make Big Statement Unai Emery Aston Villa Contract Talks Signal Stability and Serious Ambition Aston Villa have done the sensible thing. They have sat down with Unai Emery, looked at where the club is heading, and started mapping out what comes next. According to the Daily Mail , Emery is open to signing a new Aston Villa contract that could keep him at Villa Park for close to a decade. For a club trying to establish itself at the top end of English football, that matters. This is not about sentiment. It is about performance. Emery has elevated Villa, made them relevant in serious conversations again and given the project credibility. Owners can talk all they like about long-term vision, but it only carries weight if the coach delivers. Emery has done that. Aston Villa contract talks show clear direction The club confirmed discussions took place involving Emery, co-owner Nassef Sawiris, Roberto Olabe and Damian Vidagany. The official line was unmistakable: “Aston Villa held an important working meeting today to plan the club’s future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project.” That is corporate language, but the key point is simple. Villa are planning ahead, not scrambling for answers. Photo IMAGO The statement added: “The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements.” Again, straightforward enough. Villa want growth, and they want Emery leading it. Unai Emery future linked to bigger jobs That this comes amid talk of Manchester United interest is hardly surprising. Good managers attract attention. Emery, on close to £15 million a year, already sits among the Premier League’s top earners. Clubs at the highest level do not pay those sums for image, they pay them for results and structure. If United were watching, Villa’s response has been correct. Get in front of the noise, strengthen the relationship and make it clear the manager is central to the next phase. If this becomes a new deal, Villa will be sending a message. They are not here to flirt with progress. They are trying to lock it in. Our View This is exactly what everyone wanted to hear. When a manager changes the level of a club, the priority is to keep him, back him and make sure the whole structure grows around him. That is what seems to be happening here, and it feels earned. There is something hugely reassuring about seeing a proper plan. Not slogans, not chest-thumping, just a serious meeting with serious people talking about the next few years. Emery has brought standards, intelligence and consistency. Villa are stronger, sharper and far more respected because of him. The Manchester United links were always going to appear because that is what happens when a coach is doing elite work. The important thing is that Villa have acted like a club with confidence, not insecurity. There is no need to panic when the foundations are th

item.title: Diogo Reis Defends Gold Against Bebeto Oliveira, Selina Flores Faces Kana Morimoto At ONE Fight Night 50
item.description: The final U.S. primetime card of ONE Championship’s 2026 calendar, ONE Fight Night 50 on Prime Video , has been bolstered by two explosive additions. An all-Brazilian showdown awaits as ONE Flyweight Submission Grappling World Champion Diogo “Baby Shark” Reis defends his gold against multi-time BJJ World Champion Bebeto Oliveira , while Selina “Teep Queen” Flores trades blows with Kana “Krusher Queen” Morimoto in atomweight Muay Thai. The card goes down on Friday, December 18, inside Bangkok’s legendary Lumpinee Stadium. Here is a closer look at both battles. Reis Faces A Decorated Newcomer In His First Defense Photo Credit: ONE Championship Diogo Reis climbed to the top of ONE’s flyweight grappling division in only his second promotional outing, and now the reigning World Champion has a statement to make in his first defense. The two-time ADCC World Champion opened his tenure in the organization with a kimura finish of Shoya Ishiguro before following up with a stellar 10-minute display against Daiki Yonekura to claim the ONE Flyweight Submission Grappling World Title. Those performances earned him ONE’s 2025 Submission Grappler of the Year honor, and this past May he backed it up with another masterclass as he moved up to bantamweight against Yuki Takahashi , going 3-0 on the global stage. View this post on Instagram Bebeto Oliveira, though, has creativity and polish to match. The promotional debutant holds World Championship gold in both gi and no-gi competition and has beaten fellow IBJJF World Champions Edwin Ocasio, Paulo Miyao, and Thalison Soares. The matchup comes down to who controls the rhythm. “Baby Shark” wants a fast match, chaining passes into finishes, while the 32-year-old challenger is at his most dangerous when things slow down and the action sinks into his guard, where sweeps and submissions can flip the pace on even the quickest passer. Keep the exchanges moving, and Reis’ arsenal could stack up fast. Slow the match down, and Oliveira could wrap up his 2026 as the new face of the flyweight submission grappling division. Flores Looks To Spoil Kana’s Muay Thai Debut Photo Credit: ONE Championship Multi-time WBC Muay Thai World Champion Selina Flores arrived in ONE on a four-fight winning streak and stretched it to five with an impressive triumph over Marie “The Celtic Queen” McManamon in her promotional debut in October 2025. The 28-year-old’s second outing was a leap in competition, and she met it head-on. At ONE Fight Night 47 this past September, the American striker pushed former three-sport ONE World Champion Stamp Fairtex through three full rounds before losing a split decision. Her WBC titles already suggested she belongs among the best at atomweight, and taking Stamp to the scorecards in only her second promotional appearance backed that up. item.title: Harry Kane signs record-breaking Bayern Munich contract to become Europe's highest-paid player
item.description: Harry Kane signs record-breaking Bayern Munich contract to become Europe's highest-paid player Harry Kane has signed a record-breaking new contract with Bayern Munich that runs until June 2029 and is believed to make him the highest-paid player in Europe by salary. David Ornstein of The Athletic reported that the three-year extension is the most lucrative deal in Bayern's history, though some players in Europe will still earn more than Kane once bonuses are counted. The 33-year-old's previous terms were due to expire next summer. Both the player and the club were keen to extend the partnership, and Bayern do not see this as his final contract. The Bundesliga champions want to keep the England captain for the foreseeable future. “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich," Kane said in a club statement. "We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.” A remarkable few weeks for Kane The new deal caps a memorable spell for the striker. Kane won the Ballon d'Or in late October, becoming the first English player to claim the award since 2001, and he is set to become England's most-capped player during the November international break. He has scored 156 goals in 161 games since arriving from Tottenham Hotspur three years ago. In that time he has won two Bundesliga titles, the DFB-Pokal and two Supercups, while the Champions League remains his outstanding target in Munich. The commitment to Germany also means one Premier League ambition looks increasingly out of reach. Alan Shearer's all-time scoring record is now likely to elude Kane, who has opted to remain in the Bundesliga over a potential return to England.

item.title: Major Update On Mustafa Ali's TNA Future (WWE News)
item.description: TNA With regular reports that various TNA contracts have/are coming up for expiry, there's now an update on the status of Mustafa Ali . Per Fightful Select , Ali's existing TNA deal is coming up at the end of the year, with there an expectation that TNA management is eager to keep the former International Champion and X Division Champion. Fightful adds that, as one would expect, Mustafa is highly regarded by those in TNA. This report also mentions that Mustafa Ali has been "informally scouting" talent while working the independent scene, with him occasionally referring talent to TNA bosses. Of course, Leon Slater only won the TNA World Title a matter of weeks ago at Bound for Glory - defeating Nic Nemeth - so it's likely that the Youngest in Charge won't be dropping the gold anytime soon, but when he eventually does... Previously, Mustafa Ali had been with WWE from 2016 to 2023, debuting as part of the Cruiserweight Classic, becoming a staple of the burgeoning cruiserweight division, being revealed as the leader of the doomed RETRIBUTION faction, ending up back in NXT, then bizarrely released in September 2023 while being in the midst of challenging Dominik Mysterio for the NXT North American Championship. item.title: “Really Sad Seeing Novak Djokovic Losing To Basically Anyone Now” – Fans React as Shock Paris Masters Loss Seals ATP Finals Elimination
item.description: Feb 01, 2026; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; Novak Djokovic of Serbia in action against Carlos Alcaraz of Spain in the final of the men’s singles at the Australian Open at Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne Park. © Mike Frey-Imagn Images Tennis fans reacted to Novak Djokovic’s early exit at the Paris Masters, which ruled him out of contention for the ATP Finals. On Wednesday, Djokovic lost to Australian Rinky Hijikata 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 in the Round of 32, ending his hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals. The Serbian ace won the first set but struggled in the second as the qualifier broke his serve to level the match. In the deciding set, Hijikata broke Djokovic twice to secure the victory. Djokovic’s exit prompted reactions from fans, with one comparing his run to Venus Williams, who has faced 14 consecutive first-round exits this season. Since his China Open victory, Djokovic hasn’t advanced past the Round of 16. “No disrespect to Hijikata, but it’s really sad seeing Novak Djokovic losing to basically anyone now. And I’m not even a Novak fan, but it feels like the consolidation of the end of an era,” the fan wrote. Comment by u/Fun_Reflection1157 from discussion in tennis Another fan opined that Djokovic’s career is near its end and praised his legendary journey, writing: One fan suggested that Djokovic should retire, adding: Here are a few more reactions: Novak Djokovic opens up on his rivalry with Roger Federer Novak Djokovic recently spoke about his relationship with Roger Federer, stating that they never became friends because of their iconic rivalry on court. They locked horns with each other 50 times , with the Serbian leading the head-to-head score 27-23. However, Djokovic highlighted Federer’s contribution to the sport and impact on younger players. “My relationship with Roger has always been strictly professional,” Djokovic said while speaking to press in Basel . “I have always had a great deal of respect for him, and still do today, because he has contributed so much to our sport. He paved the way for younger generations, and I’m grateful to him for that. But we have never had any kind of relationship off the court. In reality, that’s only natural, given that we have always been rivals.” Djokovic and Federer first faced each other in Monte Carlo in 2006, while their semifinal match at the 2020 Australian Open was their last meeting. item.title: Career-best Wembanyama display seals Spurs win
item.description: Victor Wembanyama was the NBA's defensive player of the year last season [Getty Images] Victor Wembanyama sank the winning free throw to finish with a career-high 52 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Dallas Mavericks 112-111 on Wednesday. The French star, whose previous best was 50 points in 2024, dominated at both ends of the court to also claim 24 rebounds and eight blocks. The 22-year-old is the first player in 52 years with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in a game. He also became the fifth player since 1982 to register at least 50 points and 20 rebounds as San Antonio improved their record to 6-2. Wembanyama reached half-time with 29 points, 15 rebounds, five blocks and two steals, before the Spurs held off a second-half rally by Dallas, who were led by 29 points from Kyrie Irving. "I haven't been feeling great lately," said Wembanyama. "I've been sick for a while. "Today I felt like I got my legs back, so it should be more like this more often." James plays down Finals talk Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a 112-106 win over the Detroit Pistons in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference clash. Brown (30 points) and Embiid (26) led a balanced offensive performance as Philadelphia saw all five starters reach double figures, with LeBron James claiming a double-double of 13 points and 10 rebounds. The 76ers now have the NBA's best record at 8-1 after bringing in Brown and James in the off-season. "It's too early to be talking about the Finals and things of that nature," said James. "We'll just continue to buy into what we want to do. We got a good team." The Los Angeles Lakers beat the Sacramento Kings 116-103 with Luka Doncic scoring a game-high 40 points to reach 308 for the season. The Slovenian star became the first player to pass 300 in his first eight games of a season since Michael Jordan (303) in 1988-89. Doncic was also involved in an incident which led to a fan being removed after throwing the ball at an official, which struck her as she was signalling a Lakers possession. Meanwhile, London-born OG Anunoby scored 18 points for the New York Knicks as the reigning champions enjoyed their biggest win of the season, beating the Chicago Bulls 135-105 to improve to 4-4. item.title: Barcelona not completely ruled out of race for 16-year-old talent despite Real Madrid agreement
item.description: Barcelona not completely ruled out of race for 16-year-old talent despite Real Madrid agreement Barcelona have not completely abandoned their pursuit of Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel despite Real Madrid moving closer to securing his signature. According to SPORT , the 16-year-old forward’s future remains undecided because no contract has been signed with Los Blancos yet, leaving Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain hoping to change the situation. Real Madrid have reportedly reached a verbal agreement with Gabriel over a potential move, with the Spanish giants targeting January to bring him to the club. However, the absence of a signed contract means the other interested clubs have not entirely given up. Indeed, Real Madrid have made the most progress, although no club-to-club contact with Manchester United has taken place. Barcelona retain hope despite Real Madrid’s progress Barcelona are not completely out of JJ Gabriel race. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) According to the outlet, the teenager is attracted to Barcelona’s emphasis on developing young players and sees an opportunity to establish himself within the club’s long-term plans. Bayern Munich have also maintained contact with the player’s representatives, although their chances are more limited. PSG remain another potential destination, but Real Madrid currently appear to have the advantage following their progress in negotiations. Real Madrid’s proposal includes a multi-year contract, a significant salary, a signing bonus and agent commissions. In fact, the overall investment is understood to exceed €15 million. Real Madrid are currently winning the race. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) Notably, this is one of the biggest reasons why Barcelona have not made an official move yet, despite holding several meetings with the player’s agents . What happens now? Barcelona’s remaining opportunity could depend on whether they are prepared to reconsider their financial position. Gabriel’s attraction to the club’s development model gives Deco and the sporting department a potential advantage, but Real Madrid’s financial pull means time is becoming an important factor. For now, despite what is being said, the fact of the matter is that there is still no agreement on paper, and until then, nothing can be ruled out.

item.title: The Weekly Bobbins: One-Dimensional Reading, Lewis Wing’s (Continued) Woes
item.description: To be honest there’s not a lot to say about the Plymouth Argyle game. We should have won it. We had decent chances and looked energetic in doing so. It’s a difficult place to go to, both in terms of distance and the fixture itself, but taking a point there was no disgrace and we moved on. However, Reading’s performance against Oxford United was frankly a disgrace. What we’ve seen so far this season is enough to make a decent judgement on the team as a whole. We’ve seen enough to know that, at home, we can be flat-track bullies and have more of an edge to our game to score enough goals to win most matches. That’s where our confidence lies. But away from home, we’re a different animal completely. Aside from the MK Dons mismatch, where they were truly dismal, we show little fight, we’re timid, we look beaten as soon as we go a goal down. “The gap between the starters and the finishers is stark” Our play is one-dimensional and stale. We’ve got two out balls: one to Kyreece Lisbie and one to Jack Marriott. That’s it. That’s all we’ve got. There’s no playing between the lines or progression up the field from midfield. There’s a lot of running around but rarely do we find space. It’s so easy to counter as a result. Tie Lisbie down and that’s one avenue shafted. The returning Marriott is the only other beneficiary and he’s working off scraps. For a side that’s touted to be playoff- or promotion-worthy, it’s frankly laughable. We’ve seen the limit of this squad already, barring a huge change of attitude and commitment away from home. Further to that, it’s pretty clear that, while we have the basis of a decent starting XI, the gap between the starters and the finishers is stark. When all our players are fit, you know exactly who that starting XI is; there are no exceptions – well, there should be, but I’ll get onto that later. You can rattle that XI off right now without so much of a blink. This does come down to the manager, obviously, but either he doesn’t rate the rest of his squad that much or they aren’t that good – or both. The fact that a barely fit Marriott started against Oxford pretty much says it all. He should have been eased back into the last two games, but he started as this one meant something; the risk was worth taking. But what on earth does that say about Jacob Brown and Jamie Reid? The captain Going into central midfield is where I have my biggest beef and have done so for a couple of seasons. I never liked the pairing of Charlie Savage and Lewis Wing. They never gelled; it felt shoehorned as they were our high-value players. Now we have Andy Rinomhota and Wing together and my feelings are just the same. The common denominator is Wing. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: he’s a luxury player in a team that can’t afford luxury in that position, and this was proven last night. He’s not agile enough, he can’t tackle, he’s slow and he’s, ultimately, out for himself. He’s selfish. How many times do we have to see that same ‘half turn,

The College Football Playoff rankings put Georgia in the two spot, and Ole Miss is tenth in the first round of rankings. If Ole Miss wins, and Tennessee wins its home game over Kentucky, and South Carolina wins its home game over Texas A&M, the SEC will have a whopping ten teams that are either 5-2 or 4-3 in conference play. Or, Georgia wins, and the SEC and College Football Playoff are right there for the taking. item.title: Honda names Jake Dixon as Joan Mir's substitute for Qatar GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Honda HRC has announced that Joan Mir will be absent this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix after his comeback at Sepang was cut short due to another episode of dizziness and partial loss of vision. British rider Jake Dixon will replace the Spaniard at Losail, returning to the premier class for the first time since he competed two grands prix in 2021 as a substitute for Franco Morbidelli at Petronas SRT. He was classified 19th at Silverstone but was unable to finish the Aragon race. "Joan Mir continues his recovery process after retiring from Sunday's race in Malaysia," Honda explained in its statement. Dixon was part of the world championship paddock between 2019 and 2025, scoring seven victories and 22 podiums in Moto2. This season, the Briton moved up to Honda's factory team in the World Superbike Championship, but his season was marred by injuries. His physical recovery in the second half of the year allowed him to finish inside the top 10 on five occasions. "First of all, I want to thank Honda HRC for this opportunity," Dixon said. "Receiving the call to ride one of these bikes is something fantastic and I'm really looking forward to getting started; I think that, as children, all riders dream of competing for the official Honda MotoGP team. "It's been a while since I last rode a MotoGP bike, so we need to take the weekend calmly and go step by step. I want to wish Joan all the best and I hope to see him back on the bike very soon. It hasn't been an easy year for me either, so I can really relate to his situation. We are going to make the most of this weekend." Dixon will join Luca Marini in Honda's official factory team line-up in Qatar, after the Italian rider recovered in time to be able to travel. "Our goal for this weekend is to build on the performance we showed on Sunday at Sepang. I've been able to spend a few days at home and continue recovering, so my physical condition has improved," said the Italian. "It's a circuit that hasn't always allowed us to make the most of our strengths, but with only three races left to finish the season with Honda, this is the time to go all out and give our best in each of them. I want to wish Joan all the best; having him in the garage is always a boost for both me and the team." Dixon could finish the season in Portimao and Valencia if Mir is unable to recover. The 2020 world champion missed four races between Austria and Australia due to health issues, before returning to action in Malaysia last weekend. While he completed much of the weekend without issues after being declared fit, he was forced to retire early from the grand prix on Sunday as the same health issues resurfaced. Read Also: Jorge Martin confirms he will travel to Qatar to try to race Joan Mir says Marc Marquez’s MotoGP rivals couldn’t cope with title pressure To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Jason Whitlock accuses LeBron James of influencing Bryce’s role after Arizona debut
item.description: Photo by Harry How/Getty Images Jason Whitlock has questioned Bryce James’ place in Arizona’s basketball team after LeBron James’ youngest son made his first start for the Wildcats. The veteran analyst believes LeBron’s influence, rather than Bryce’s performances, may have played a part in him receiving an opportunity with the college programme. Bryce featured for just six minutes in Arizona’s 84-75 upset defeat to UCLA, recording no points or rebounds and finishing with one assist. Jason Whitlock questions Bryce James’ role with Arizona Whitlock was particularly critical of the limited role Bryce was given during the game and suggested his involvement was more about keeping his father happy than his ability on the court. Speaking in an Instagram video, Whitlock said: “Bryce James is a make-a-swish kid. Arizona, the number 5 team country last night, gave Bryce James, LeBron’s youngest son, three minutes at the beginning of the first half and three minutes at the beginning of the second half, and that’s it.” He then made his criticism of LeBron’s influence even clearer: “He’s a make-a-swish kid, has no business on the Arizona basketball team, and LeBron is forcing them to give him token starts.” Bryce went 0-for-3 from the field and missed both of his three-point attempts against UCLA. However, it was only his first appearance and does not necessarily reflect what he can offer Arizona over the course of the season. The youngster redshirted his freshman year to preserve his eligibility while developing his game and adjusting to college basketball. His brother Bronny also faced scrutiny during his only season at USC, where he averaged 4.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists. Whitlock has previously questioned LeBron’s decisions regarding Bronny’s basketball career. He suggested the Lakers star could have encouraged his eldest son to pursue American football instead. “Bronny James, with a different father, would be an outside linebacker or free safety on a major college football team, seen as a first- or second-round draft pick,” he said. Bryce now has time to respond to the criticism and establish himself at Arizona. His performances in the coming games will be important as he looks to build his own reputation rather than simply being viewed as LeBron James’ son. item.title: Harry Kane extends deal with Bayern until 2029
item.description: Bayern Munich's Harry Kane attends a press conference, ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League soccer match against Atletico Madrid. (is associated with: «Harry Kane extends deal with Bayern until 2029») David Canales/dpa Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane says he feels "right at home" after signing a contract extension at Bayern Munich. The England captain, 33, took the game's top individual honour last week after a record-breaking stint with the Bundesliga giants and has now recommitted to the club until June 2029. Since arriving from Tottenham in 2023, Kane has scored a remarkable 156 goals in 161 appearances, winning two league titles and three domestic cups. Speaking after penning his new deal, he said: "I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. "We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. "My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. "I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club."

item.title: 3 Takeaways as Victor Wembanyama's career night helps Spurs clip Dallas
item.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) dunks the ball in a game against the Dallas Mavericks at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Dallas Mavericks 112-111. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Victor Wembanyama took one look at the stat sheet after the Spurs' thrilling 112-111 victory over Dallas on Wednesday and decided he had left a few things on the table. Fifty-two points, a career high. Twenty-four rebounds, another career high. Nineteen free throws. You guessed it. Another career high. His eight blocks weren't a career high, but they weren't exactly shabby, either. After authoring a statistical masterpiece that would have made even Wilt Chamberlain do a double-take, Wembanyama still wasn't impressed with himself. "I can be much better," he said. True, Wembanyama missed 7 of 8 3-point tries. He clanged four straight free throws in the fourth quarter, after making 18 in a row to start the game. Other than that? "He was Superman," Spurs guard Dylan Harper said. Dylan Harper on some of the highlight plays Victor Wembanyama made against the Mavs tonight: https://t.co/0Q7adBN9K4 - Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation) November 5, 2026 With the rest of the team laboring through one of its toughest shooting nights of the season, the Spurs needed their All-Star center to come charging out of the phone booth to save them. Wembanyama was happy to oblige. Again and again. With Wembanyama destroying Dallas' best-laid plans on both ends, the Spurs managed to hold on for their fifth consecutive victory. Dylan Harper added 21 points for the Spurs, while Stephon Castle supplied a hard-earned 17 points and 10 rebounds despite a 6-for-20 shooting night. "Obviously Victor's numbers reflect a wow game," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "But I thought we had some really, really tough winning plays all over the board tonight." The Spurs' winning streak began Oct. 24, with a 122-106 triumph in Dallas. Neither All-Star guard Kyrie Irving nor reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg played for the Mavericks in that one. They were both available Wednesday, facing the Spurs together for the first time. Irving ended with 29 points, but missed a heavily contested 15-foot jumper at the final horn that would have given Dallas the win. Flagg, who was coming off a dreadful 3-of-19 performance in Dallas' loss to lowly Sacramento, started 1-of-11 against the Spurs. He salvaged his night in the second half, finishing 7 of 19 for 19 points with 10 rebounds. Naji Marshall added 22 points off the bench for the Mavs, including 10 during a fourth-quarter spurt that allowed Dallas to tie the game after trailing by as many as 19. None of it was enough to overcome Wembanyama's magnum opus. "When he plays like that, you see the result," Harper said. item.title: La Liga icon launches scathing criticism of Vinicius and Real Madrid: ‘Incapable of justifying his status’
item.description: La Liga icon launches scathing criticism of Vinicius and Real Madrid: ‘Incapable of justifying his status’ Former Real Madrid goalkeeper Santiago Canizares has delivered a scathing assessment of Vinicius Jr., arguing that the Brazilian has struggled to move on from losing the 2024 Ballon d’Or. He also questioned Real Madrid’s decision to boycott the awards ceremony in Paris that year, believing the club’s response contributed to the status and expectations surrounding their forward. Speaking on Movistar Plus Deportes’ La Casa del Fútbol (h/t SPORT ), Canizares identified the Ballon d’Or disappointment as a defining moment in Vinicius’ recent behaviour. The former goalkeeper, who represented Real Madrid between 1988 and 1992 and again from 1994 to 1998, argued that the club’s public backing of the player has also influenced the situation. Canizarez has launched fresh criticism towards Vinicius. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “What has hit Vinicius the hardest is missing out on that Ballon d’Or and finding himself in a situation where a club bends to his will and does not travel to the Ballon d’Or ceremony,” said Canizares. Canizares questions the treatment Vinicius receives at Real Madrid Canizares believes Real Madrid’s decision to publicly support Vinicius after the Ballon d’Or outcome created expectations that the forward has subsequently struggled to justify through his performances. He then questioned the influence of that episode on the Brazilian’s perception of his standing at the club, adding: “These are things that don’t come naturally, and now Vini thinks he has a certain status, which he does have contractually…” Vinicius is not enjoying the best run of form this season. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “Now Mourinho has to step in to defend Vinicius at every press conference.” Canizares questions Vinicius’ performances Canizares ultimately believes that Vinicius must demonstrate his importance through his performances rather than rely on the reputation and contractual standing he enjoys at Madrid. He concluded his assessment with a particularly direct criticism of the Brazilian’s current contribution, stating, “Vinicius is incapable of justifying that status on the pitch.”

item.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
item.description: President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028. The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss. But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama. – Republicans in turmoil – The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb. Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterms campaigns with rallies in swing states. The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday. But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump. It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden. “The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations, said. Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about. Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war. The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal. He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off. Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state. – Democrats on a high – The Democratic field is crowded but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost. Ossoff’s reelection as Georgia Senator has fueled speculation about a 2028 run by a telegenic politician who has already gained attention for mocking Trump’s relationship with a young staffer. The 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for president” but his swiftly-declared win in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his status in the party.
